title: How the queen moves
outcomes: Taps every square a queen can reach, stopping in front of its own pieces and on the first enemy piece
Rejects a knight-shaped jump for the queen
Tells whether a blocker on one line affects the queen's other lines

steps.text: The **queen** is the strongest piece. She moves like a rook and a bishop combined: any distance along a rank, a file or a diagonal. She cannot jump, and she captures the same way: by landing on an enemy piece. That gives her eight lines out of her square.

steps.caption: Eight directions. Two white pawns and two black pawns decide where each line stops.

steps.text: **When it holds:** the queen slides along any of her eight lines until something stops her. A friendly piece stops her one square early; an enemy piece can be captured, and she stops there. **When it fails:** she never moves like a knight, and she cannot jump over anything. Each line is blocked separately, so a blocker on one line leaves the other seven alone.
